note: Spain finding (reviewer ruling on #23): in-sample, one race, no CI. none is flattered only through the SC factor (sc_lap_factor 1.36 was set on this race); the base delta is a common level the offset adjustment removes. The shrinkage loss at horizon 40-49 (k 17-26) is the first-stint wear/fuel identifiability window documented in #14. The losses at 10-39 suggest the race-fitted linear MEDIUM wear (0.068, pulled up by old-tyre curvature a linear model cannot represent) predicts remaining stints worse than the practice value (0.031): this points at the hinge degradation model for sprint 2, not at the shrinkage. Nothing is changed on Spain; taus, hinge and calibrator choice are selected across races by LORO. This is not evidence that race evidence hurts in general.

Spain finding (reviewer ruling on #26): in-sample, one race, no CI. degradation linear_fuel_hinge (knot 25, hinge tau 0.05). With the hinge the race-fitted MEDIUM wear (0.033, sd 0.007) agrees with the practice value (0.031): the linear model's 0.068 was old-tyre curvature read as slope, and the full-fit residual in the 30-40 tyre-age bin falls from 0.76 to 0.04. That vindicates the practice wear as the to_snapshot prior. It does not close the shrinkage-vs-none gap at horizons 20-40 (15.38 vs 8.97), so that gap is not curvature; the 40-49 loss (36) sits in the first-stint window where wear and fuel are separated by the priors alone. Practice never passes age 25 on Spain, so the hinge prior is 0. Nothing is changed on Spain; the degradation model, taus and calibrator are selected across races by LORO.
